'''Francisco José Ynduráin Muñoz''' (23 December 1940 – 6 June 2008) was a Spanish [[theoretical physicist]]. He founded the [[particle physics]] research group that became the Department of Theoretical Physics at the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]], where he was a professor.<ref>[http://www.ft.uam.es] Department of Theoretical Physics at the Autonomous University of Madrid.</ref> He was described by his colleagues as "a scientist that always searched for excellence in research".<ref>Antonio González Arroyo and J. L. Sánchez Gómez, "[http://www.elpais.com/articulo/Necrologicas/investigador/cientifico/siempre/busco/excelencia/elpepinec/20080607elpepinec_2/Tes Un investigador científico que siempre buscó la excelencia]", ''El País'', 7 June 2008 (accessed 9 October 2008).</ref>

==Early life==
Yndurain was born in [[Benavente, Zamora|Benavente]] in the [[Province of Zamora]] and grew up in [[Zaragoza]]. After graduating from Zaragoza's San Agustin High school, he received his M.S. degree in [[mathematics]] in 1962 and in 1964 his PhD in physics. He obtained both degrees from the [[University of Zaragoza]] (Spain).

While completing his doctoral studies, he was a visiting scientist at [[CERN]] and a Teaching Assistant at the University of Zaragoza (Spain).

==Career==
Ynduráin was an associate professor at the University of Zaragoza until 1966. He was a researcher at [[New York University]] from 1966 to 1968, at which point he moved to Geneva to become a research fellow at CERN until 1970. He was a researcher at CERN from then on, as a senior scientific associate (1976–1992), and as a member of the scientific policy committee (1988–1994).

In 1970, he took the professor position in [[Madrid]] (at the [[Complutense University]] and immediately after at the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]]) where he founded and headed the Particle Physics Research group.<ref>Martinus J. G. Veltman, [http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/1999/veltman-autobio.html Nobel Prize Autobiography].</ref> He was director of the Department of Theoretical Physics (1974–1977 and 1981–1984), dean of the Faculty of Science (1975) and deputy president (1978–1981) of the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]].

He also held other short-term appointments at other universities worldwide:
* [[Central University of Venezuela]] in Caracas, Venezuela (1967).
* [[Paris-Sud 11 University]], Paris, France (1969 and 1970).
* [[University of Groningen]], Netherlands (1973).
* [[Aix-Marseille University|Université de Marseille]], [[Marseille]], France (1979, 1980, 1981 and 1982)
* [[University of Michigan]], [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], USA (1987, 1988, 1991, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1997 and 2001).
* [[National University of La Plata]], Argentina (1994).
* [[Princeton University]], New Jersey, USA (2008).

He collaborated with other research centers:
* [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (1984).
* National Institute for Nuclear Physics and High Energy Physics [[NIKHEF]], 1997 and 2001).
* Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (1980 and 1982).
* Centro latinoamericano de Física in Bogotá, Colombia (1985, 1986 and 1987).<ref>[http://www.cbpf.br/~claf/index2.html Centro lationamericano de Física] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090411190441/http://www.cbpf.br/~claf/index2.html |date=11 April 2009 }}.</ref>

He was a member of the Royal Spanish Physical Society,<ref>[http://www.rsef.org/ Royal Spanish Physical Society].</ref> Royal Academy of Exact Physical and Natural Sciences of Spain,<ref>[http://www.rac.es/ Royal Academy of Exact Physical and Natural Sciences of Spain]</ref> where he was president of the Physics and Chemistry section from 2002 to 2006. He was also member of the [[American Physical Society]], founding member of the [[European Physical Society]] and member of the European Academy of Sciences energy committee. In 2004 he was nominated general secretary of the Instituto de España.

==Works==
In 1983, Yndurain published a widely used book advanced textbook on [[quantum field theory]] for graduate students, ''Quantum Chromodynamics: An Introduction to the Theory of Quarks and Gluons''.<ref>{{cite book | last=Ynduráin | first=F.J. | title=Quantum Chromodynamics: An Introduction to the Theory of Quarks and Gluons | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | series=Theoretical and Mathematical Physics | year=2013 | isbn=978-3-662-09633-8 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9e_tCAAAQBAJ |postscript=; pbk reprint of 1983 1st edition}}</ref> The book has been translated into Russian as ''Kvantovaia Khromodinamika''. The book was expanded twice: once in 1990 in Spanish as ''Mecánica Cuántica Relativista'' and translated into English in 1996 as ''Relativistic Quantum Mechanics and Introduction to Field Theory'' (with a later revised translation),<ref>{{cite book | last=Ynduráin | first=F.J. | title=Relativistic Quantum Mechanics and Introduction to Field Theory | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | series=Theoretical and Mathematical Physics | year=2012 | isbn=978-3-642-61057-8 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jLD0CAAAQBAJ }}</ref> and again in 1999 as ''The Theory of Quark and Gluon Interactions'' (with several later editions).<ref>{{cite book | last=Ynduráin | first=F.J. | title=The Theory of Quark and Gluon Interactions | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | series=Theoretical and Mathematical Physics | year=2007 | isbn=978-3-540-33210-7 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8u3-RKly2MsC | edition=4th}}</ref>

Yndurain also wrote books on science for a broader audience. In 1997, he published a book discussing [[UFOs]] theories, ''Quién anda ahí?'', which won the Golondriz award for smart humor in 1998. In 2002, he published a book about the structure of matter entitled ''Electrones, neutrinos y quarks''. Finally, in 2004 he published a book about science, scientists and history entitled ''Los desafíos de la ciencia''.<ref>{{cite book | last=Ynduráin | first=F.J. | title=Los desafíos de la ciencia: Diez ensayos sobre la ciencia, los científicos y la historia | publisher=Crítica | series=Drakontos Series | year=2003 | isbn=978-84-8432-473-7 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=W17gXpcdhpIC | language=es }}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1986: Nominated Cavaliere Ufficiale nell'Ordine al Merito, one of the main [[Italian orders of merit]].
* 1990: Annual Award of the Royal Spanish Academy of Sciences.
* 1992: Elected Member of the Spanish Royal Academy of Exact, Physical and Natural Sciences.<ref>[http://www.rac.es/ ''Royal Academy of Exact, Physical and Natural Sciences''].</ref>
* 1994: Nominated Distinguished Guest by the University of La Plata
* 1995: Elected member of European Academy of Sciences and Arts
* 2001: Nominated member of The World Innovation Foundation.<ref>[http://www.thewif.org.uk/ The World Innovation Foundation].</ref>
* 2003: Gold medal for scientific excellence of the Spanish Academy of Physics.

Francisco Ynduráin Muñoz (1940–2008)]", 1 July 2008 (accessed 10 October 2008).</ref> He authored or co-authored more than 100 scientific papers on [[high energy physics]], [[nuclear physics]] and [[mathematical physics]].
